published.citation: Patel et al. 2026, dayside brightness temperature fitted with the geometric albedo to the TESS and CHEOPS occultation depths: 3121 +/- 181 K, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026A&A...706A..75P/abstract

temperature.note: Its day side's brightness temperature is measured in secondary eclipse in the TESS and CHEOPS bands together (TESS and CHEOPS) and nobody has imaged it, so the color is a Planck spectrum at its published temperature.
temperature.chosen: the paper's own value (+145, -181 K; the larger is kept), with reflected light fitted (geometric albedo 0.24 ± 0.07) under a flat albedo spectrum the paper says may not be correct; Lendl et al. 2020 (3,348 K) and Deline et al. 2022 (3,542 K) assume the planet reflects no light
temperature.band: the TESS and CHEOPS bands together
